title: Rewriting exponential expressions
keyIdea: Exponent laws let you rewrite an exponential so its base shows the rate for a different period, without changing the function: aᵗ = (a^(1/n))^(nt) = (aᵏ)^(t/k). So 1.15ᵗ ≈ 1.0117^(12t) shows 15% a year as about 1.17% a month, and 2^(t/3) ≈ 1.26ᵗ shows a 3-year doubling time as 26% a year. Rates for a new period come from roots and powers of the growth factor, never from dividing or multiplying the percentage.

kid: An exponential like y = 1.15ᵗ grows by 15% each year. The base 1.15 is the growth factor for one year. You can rewrite the same function so its base shows the rate for a month, a quarter or two years. The graph stays the same.
The key law is (aᵐ)ⁿ = a^(mn). So 1.15ᵗ = (1.15^(1/12))^(12t). Work out 1.15^(1/12) ≈ 1.0117. That gives 1.15ᵗ ≈ 1.0117^(12t), which is about 1.17% a month.
The trap is to divide the rate. 15 ÷ 12 = 1.25% a month looks right, but 1.0125¹² ≈ 1.161. That is 16.1% a year, which is too much. Growth on growth means each month needs a bit less than 1.25%.

Going the other way, raise the factor to a power. 1% a month gives 1.01¹² ≈ 1.1268, so 12.68% a year, not 12%. A law like 2^(t/3) doubles every 3 years. Rewrite it as (2^(1/3))ᵗ ≈ 1.26ᵗ to get 26% a year.
adult: This A-level topic (ages 16 to 18) uses the laws of indices to rewrite exponential functions so that the base shows the growth or decay rate for a chosen period. The identity aᵗ = (a^(1/n))^(nt) = (aᵏ)^(t/k) changes the period without changing the function or its graph. It builds on graphs of exponential functions and leads into compound interest, half-life and modelling questions.

The method has two directions. To shorten the period, take a root of the growth factor: 15% a year gives a monthly factor of 1.15^(1/12) ≈ 1.0117. To lengthen it, raise the factor to a power: 1% a month gives 1.01¹² ≈ 1.1268 a year. Doubling and half-life laws work the same way, so 2^(t/3) = (2^(1/3))ᵗ ≈ 1.26ᵗ and 0.5^(t/8) has a daily factor of about 0.917.

Common mistakes: dividing the annual percentage by 12 to get a monthly rate; multiplying a monthly rate by 12 to get an annual one; adding 15% and 15% for two years instead of squaring 1.15; squaring the rate 0.15 instead of the factor 1.15; and changing the exponent without changing the base, as in 1.15^(12t). Be careful to round only at the end, since 1.0117 is already an approximation.

In the lab learners drag a monthly factor until twelve months make ×1.15, compound 1% a month month by month, read the yearly factor off the curve of 2^(t/3), sort six forms by whether they equal 1.15ᵗ, and convert a yearly rate to any period on one unchanged curve.

practice.prompt: y = 1.15ᵗ, with t in years. Which form shows the monthly rate?
practice.hint: The monthly factor m must satisfy m¹² = 1.15, so m = 1.15^(1/12).

practice.prompt: A quantity grows by {=10*r}% each year. By what percentage does it grow over 2 years?
practice.hint: Square the growth factor 1 + {=r/10}, do not double the rate.
practice.explain: The 2-year factor is (1 + {=r/10})² = 1 + {=2*r/10} + {=r*r/100}, so the growth over 2 years is {=20*r+r*r}%.

practice.prompt: y = {b}^(2t). Write it as y = cᵗ. What is c?
A loan grows by 1% each month. Which is its yearly growth factor?
practice.hint: Twelve months means multiplying by 1.01 twelve times.
practice.explain: 1.01^(12t) = (1.01¹²)ᵗ ≈ 1.1268ᵗ, so the yearly rate is 12.68%, a bit more than 12% because of growth on growth.

practice.prompt: y = 1.21ᵗ. Write it as y = k^(2t). What is k?
practice.hint: You need k² = 1.21, so take the square root.
practice.explain: k^(2t) = (k²)ᵗ, so k² = 1.21 and k = 1.1. The rate is 10% per half-period and 21% per whole period.

pool.prompt: Why is 1.0125^(12t) not the same function as 1.15ᵗ?
pool.hint: Work out the yearly factor of 1.0125^(12t).
pool.explain: 1.0125^(12t) = (1.0125¹²)ᵗ ≈ 1.161ᵗ, which is 16.1% a year. Dividing 15% by 12 ignores growth on growth.

pool.prompt: y = 3^(t/{k}), with t in years. Every how many years does y triple?
pool.hint: y triples when the exponent t/{k} goes up by 1.
pool.explain: 3^(t/{k}) = (3^(1/{k}))ᵗ, and t/{k} increases by 1 every {k} years, so y triples every {k} years.

pool.prompt: y = {=q*q}^(t/2). Write it as y = cᵗ. What is c?
pool.hint: (a)^(t/2) = (a^(1/2))ᵗ: take the square root of the base.

pool.prompt: y = 2^(t/5), with t in years. What is the yearly growth factor?
pool.explain: 2^(t/5) = (2^(1/5))ᵗ ≈ 1.149ᵗ, so it grows about 14.9% a year and doubles every 5 years.

pool.prompt: A sample decays as y = 100 × 0.5^(t/8), with t in days. What happens each day?
pool.hint: The half-life is 8 days. Rewrite as (0.5^(1/8))ᵗ.
pool.explain: 0.5^(t/8) = (0.5^(1/8))ᵗ ≈ 0.917ᵗ, so about 8.3% is lost each day. Dividing 50% by 8 ignores decay on decay.

pool.prompt: A quantity grows by {=10*r}% a year. By what percentage does it grow over 3 years? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
y = 1.0125^(12t), with t in years. What is the yearly percentage rate, to 1 decimal place?
pool.hint: Find the yearly factor 1.0125¹², then subtract 1.
pool.explain: 1.0125¹² ≈ 1.1608, so the yearly rate is about 16.1%, not 15%.

pool.prompt: Which form is the same function as 1.2ᵗ?
pool.hint: Square the factor for a 2-year period, and halve the exponent.
pool.explain: 1.44^(t/2) = (1.2²)^(t/2) = 1.2ᵗ. 1.4 adds 20% twice, and 1.2^(2t) grows 20% every half year.

visual.caption: Is each form the same function as 1.2ᵗ? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.
